cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guillaumeloulier-PhpstormProjects-oss-elephc--claude-worktrees-streams-csv-signature/c8dbe38f-1f79-484f-9b83-62bacab9ca56/scratchpad/uv/msg34.txt <<'EOF'
fix(streams): file_put_contents() joins an array payload instead of refusing to compile

    file_put_contents("a.txt", ["a", "b", "c"]);
    → EIR backend error: unsupported EIR backend feature:
          file_put_contents data for PHP type Array(Str)

php does not CAST the array — `(string)$array` is `"Array"` with a notice. It concatenates each
element's ordinary string conversion with no separator, which is exactly `implode("", $data)`.
MEASURED on `php -n` 8.5.6: `["a","b","c"]` writes `"abc"` and returns 3, `[1, 2.5, true, null]`
writes `"12.51"` and returns 5 (`true` → `"1"`, `null` → `""`), and `[]` writes nothing and
returns 0.

That is why the join belongs to this builtin rather than to the shared string loader, whose
refusal is correct for everything else: an array reaching a string context anywhere else really
does become `"Array"`.

`__rt_implode` already leaves its result in the string result registers, which is where every write
route reads the payload from, so the array case needs nothing after it.

EIGHT call sites, not six. The wrapper, compress and phar routes take the payload in
`phar_write.rs`; the ORDINARY filesystem writer takes it in `seek_hash_arch.rs`, which is the path
a plain `file_put_contents($p, $array)` actually reaches — fixing only the first six left the
common case failing exactly as before, which is how the miss was caught.
EOF
